claim.pdf_says: In the ACCESS MODE general format the level-2 box encloses only DYNAMIC, inside the inner braces: the inner right brace closes after the box, exactly as the same format is drawn on page 438 (VIII-8).
claim.why_it_matters: The level-2 box marker and the inner closing brace are misnested (box opens before DYNAMIC but closes after the inner brace), so the figure shows the inner brace inside the box; page 438's copy of the same format has it right: '║ <u>DYNAMIC</u> ║ ╯'. The choice structure is unchanged, but the delimiter nesting is wrong.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (VIII-10, 2.4.2) shows ACCESS MODE IS { SEQUENTIAL [RELATIVE KEY IS data-name-1] | {RANDOM / [DYNAMIC boxed]} RELATIVE KEY IS data-name-1 }: the box encloses only the word DYNAMIC and the inner right brace follows the box. The markdown line 18 is '╰ ╰ ║ <u>DYNAMIC</u> ╯ ║ ... ╯', so the claim quotes it correctly and the glyph order of the box's closing bar and the inner brace's closing corner is indeed swapped. But nothing the figure says changes: the box still marks exactly the word DYNAMIC as a level-2 element, the inner braces still stack RANDOM over DYNAMIC as a choose-exactly-one alternative before RELATIVE KEY IS data-name-1, and the outer braces still choose between the SEQUENTIAL and RANDOM/DYNAMIC lines. The box encloses no other syntactic element, so the swap of two closing glyphs on one line is a drawing-order artifact. The claim itself says 'the choice structure is unchanged'. Under the rule that a difference that does not change meaning is rejected, this is not a content discrepancy.
verdict.corrected_description: Cosmetic glyph-order slip in the drawing: on the DYNAMIC line, the box's closing bar is drawn after the inner closing brace corner ('║ DYNAMIC ╯ ║') where the PDF draws the box closing first ('║ DYNAMIC ║ ╯'). The level-2 marking (DYNAMIC only) and the brace choice structure are the same in both sources.
